name: Bally Ribbon Mills
old_description: Design, development, and manufacturer of specialized engineered woven webbing, tapes, and specialty fabrics.
about:
Founded in 1923 in Bally, Pennsylvania, Bally Ribbon Mills (BRM) has operated as a privately held manufacturer of engineered narrow fabrics for over a century. The company began producing specialized woven webbing, tapes, and specialty fabrics for critical-use applications.

BRM designs, develops, and manufactures a range of woven products including narrow tapes, webbing, seamless tubular materials, 2-D and 3-D structural shapes, braided structures, and multi-layer complex fabrics. Production methods encompass shuttle looms, needle looms, Jacquard looms, braiding equipment, and specialty broadlooms capable of widths up to 72 inches. Post-weave processes include dyeing, finishing (heat setting, resin treating, PTFE, silicone, flame retardant), strap cutting, hole punching, and sonic welding. The facility supports prototype through full-scale production runs.

The company serves aerospace, defense, medical (Class I–III devices, orthopedic, prosthetic, and dental biotextiles), safety (firefighting protective clothing per NFPA and Canadian standards), automotive, commercial, industrial, and composites markets. Customers include OEMs, medical device manufacturers, defense contractors, and safety equipment suppliers requiring Berry Amendment–compliant materials.

BRM differentiates itself through an engineering team credited with pioneering 3-D weaving technology, the ability to weave virtually any yarn—from nylons and polyesters to aramids, graphite, ceramics, and silicon carbide—and a 24/7 in-house quality laboratory. The quality system is certified to ISO 9001:2015, AS9100D, and ISO 13485:2016, with TS 16949 compliance for automotive customers.
